Local Gyrification Index

Exploratory Analyses

Author

Zachary Heffernan

Published

October 1, 2026

Main Effects

  • There is a significant nonlinear effect of Age on Global LGI, where Global LGI declines with Age.
  • There is a significant positive correlation between Socioeconomic Status and Global LGI.
  • There is a significant nonlinear effect of Trauma Exposure on Global LGI, where those with higher Trauma Exposure have lower Global LGI.
  • There is a significant difference in Global LGI between sexes, with Males having higher Global LGI than Females.
  • There is a significant decreasing trend in Global LGI across increasing levels of GOASSESS Psychosis Scores.

Global LGI ~ Age

Global LGI is significantly negatively correlated with age. This effect is significantly nonlinear, though the nonlinearity is subtle.

data_lgi_age <-
  inner_join(global_lgi, demo, by = c("bblid")) |>
  select(lgi, age) |>
  drop_na()

test_lgi_age <-
  cor.test(data_lgi_age$lgi, data_lgi_age$age)

plot_lgi_age <-
  ggplot(data = data_lgi_age, aes(x = age, y = lgi)) +
  geom_point() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation of Global LGI and Age",
    subtitle = report_correlation(test_lgi_age),
    x = "Age",
    y = "LGI (global)"
  )

plot_lgi_age

Global LGI ~ s(Age)

model_lgi_age <- gam(
  lgi ~ age + s(age, m = c(2, 0)),
  data = data_lgi_age,
  method = "REML"
)

summary(model_lgi_age)

Family: gaussian 
Link function: identity 

Formula:
lgi ~ age + s(age, m = c(2, 0))

Parametric coefficients:
             Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
(Intercept)  3.517750   0.084635  41.564  < 2e-16 ***
age         -0.018266   0.005642  -3.238  0.00123 ** 
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

Approximate significance of smooth terms:
         edf Ref.df     F p-value   
s(age) 2.232      8 1.054 0.00863 **
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

R-sq.(adj) =  0.314   Deviance explained = 31.5%
-REML = -932.97  Scale est. = 0.017064  n = 1533
plot_lgi_age_linearity <- ggplot(data = data_lgi_age, aes(x = age, y = lgi)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    formula = y ~ x,
    se = FALSE,
    aes(color = "Linear")
  ) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "gam",
    formula = y ~ s(x),
    se = FALSE,
    aes(color = "Nonlinear")
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Linear" = "blue", "Nonlinear" = "red"),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  labs(
    title = "Linearity of Relationship Between Global LGI and Age",
    x = "Age",
    y = "LGI (global)"
  )

plot_lgi_age_linearity

Global LGI ~ Socioeconomic Status

Global LGI is signitifantly positively correlated with socioeconomic status. This effect is not significantly nonlinear.

  inner_join(global_lgi, env, by = "bblid") |>
  select(lgi, env_ses) |>
  drop_na()

  geom_point() +
  theme_minimal() +

    subtitle = report_correlation(test_lgi_ses),
    x = "Socioeconomic Status",
    y = "LGI (global)"

Global LGI ~ Trauma Exposure

Global LGI ~ Sex

There are significant differences in Global LGI between sexes, with Males having higher Global LGI than Females.

data_lgi_sex <-
  inner_join(global_lgi, demo, by = "bblid") |>
  select(lgi, sex) |>
  drop_na()

test_lgi_sex <-
  t.test(lgi ~ sex, data = data_lgi_sex)

plot_lgi_sex <-
  ggplot(data = data_lgi_sex, aes(x = sex, y = lgi, color = sex, fill = sex)) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.5) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  color_scale_sex +
  fill_scale_sex +
  labs(
    title = "Differences in Global LGI between Sexes",
    subtitle = report_t_test(test_lgi_sex),
    x = "Sex",
    y = "LGI (global)"
  )

plot_lgi_sex

Global LGI ~ GOASSESS Psychosis Category

Global LGI shows a significant decreasing trend across increasing levels of GOASSESS Psychosis Scores.

data_lgi_psy <-
  inner_join(global_lgi, goassess, by = c("bblid" = "subject_id")) |>
  select(lgi, smry_psy_cat) |>
  filter(smry_psy_cat %in% c(0, 1, 2, 3, 4)) |>
  mutate(smry_psy_cat = ordered(smry_psy_cat)) |>
  drop_na()

test_lgi_psy <-
  clinfun::jonckheere.test(
    x = data_lgi_psy$lgi,
    g = data_lgi_psy$smry_psy_cat,
    alternative = "decreasing"
  )

plot_lgi_psy <-
  ggplot(
    data = data_lgi_psy,
    aes(x = smry_psy_cat, y = lgi, color = smry_psy_cat, fill = smry_psy_cat)
  ) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.5) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  scale_x_discrete(
    labels = c(
      "0" = "Not Endorsed",
      "1" = "Endorsed",
      "2" = "Subthreshold",
      "3" = "Threshold",
      "4" = "Significant"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Differences in Global LGI between Psychosis Categories",
    subtitle = report_jt(test_lgi_psy),
    x = "GOASSESS Psychosis Category",
    y = "LGI (global)"
  )

plot_lgi_psy

Two-Way Interactions

  • There are no significant linear or nonlinear interactions between age and sex. The most complex model supported is lgi ~ s(age) + sex.

Global LGI ~ Age * Sex

data_lgi_age_sex <-
  inner_join(global_lgi, demo, by = c("bblid")) |>
  mutate(
    sex_ord = ordered(sex, levels = c("Female", "Male")),
    age_c = age - mean(age)
  ) |>
  select(lgi, age, age_c, sex, sex_ord) |>
  drop_na()

Global LGI ~ Sex + Age + s(Age, m = c(2,0))

Sex contributes when accounting for age. Age contributes when accounting for sex, and this effect is significantly nonlinear.

model_lgi_age_sex_1 <- gam(
  lgi ~ sex + age_c + s(age_c, m = c(2, 0)),
  data = data_lgi_age_sex,
  method = "REML"
)

summary(model_lgi_age_sex_1)

Family: gaussian 
Link function: identity 

Formula:
lgi ~ sex + age_c + s(age_c, m = c(2, 0))

Parametric coefficients:
             Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
(Intercept)  3.198785   0.004284  746.69  < 2e-16 ***
sexMale      0.096194   0.006246   15.40  < 2e-16 ***
age_c       -0.019361   0.004588   -4.22 2.59e-05 ***
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

Approximate significance of smooth terms:
           edf Ref.df     F p-value   
s(age_c) 1.934      8 1.016 0.00668 **
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

R-sq.(adj) =  0.405   Deviance explained = 40.7%
-REML = -1039.1  Scale est. = 0.014791  n = 1533

Global LGI ~ Sex * Age + s(Age, m = c(2,0))
